MVSNeRF is a method for fast, generalizable radiance field reconstruction from multi-view stereo that learns a data prior to bypass per-scene optimization [S1][S2, unofficial].

The claim states that MVSNeRF is a method for fast, generalizable radiance field reconstruction from multi-view stereo that learns a data prior to bypass per-scene optimization. Source [S1] confirms the method extracts 2D features, maps them to a 3D cost volume, uses a 3D CNN for encoding, and jointly optimizes the volume and MLP, noting it reaches results comparable to hours of baseline NeRF training within 15 minutes (supporting 'fast'). Source [S2] explicitly states that MVSNeRF uses a 'feedforward model to learn data prior' and that this 'accelerates convergence' (supporting 'learns a data prior' and 'fast'). The title in [S2] also includes 'Fast Generalizable Radiance Field Reconstruction from Multi-View Stereo'. The phrase 'bypass per-scene optimization' is supported by the description of using a feedforward model and learning a data prior to accelerate convergence, which implies avoiding the slow iterative optimization typical of standard NeRF.
